    A band brick gives infinitely many bricks #

    On the common space X = k^n, the endomorphisms of M(b, t) are the kernel of the commutator map with the vertex and arrow actions. After multiplying the arrow part by t, this map is polynomial in t (T_eq). By semicontinuity, if M(b, λ) is a brick then so is M(b, t) for all but finitely many t (finite_not_isBrick). These are pairwise non-isomorphic, so a primitive band brick contradicts brick-finiteness (not_isBrickFinite).
